title: Non-Desarguesian Planes: The Moulton Plane Counterexample

problemStatement.plain: Construct a concrete non-Desarguesian plane (the Moulton plane) in Lean and exhibit a counterexample to Desargues's theorem.
whyMatters: Demonstrates Desargues is a property of incidence structure, not just point sets
Connects to coordinatizability: Desarguesian iff coordinatizable by division ring
Complements OQ-01 which proved Desargues over all CommRings

proven: Moulton plane definitions (MLine, onLine) over Q
Perspectivity from point O for concrete triangle pair
Three Moulton intersection points computed and verified
Non-collinearity by exhaustive case analysis over MLine constructors
knownResults.goal: Formalize the Moulton plane and prove Desargues fails

builtItems: onLine incidence relation with piecewise slope doubling
bent_left/bent_right helper theorems for incidence proofs
Concrete counterexample: O=(-4,12), ABC, A'B'C' all at x<=0
insights: Moulton lines over Q give exact arithmetic - norm_num closes all goals
Key: only ONE side line (CA, slope -1/2) needs to cross y-axis with negative slope
All vertices at x <= 0 ensures perspectivity lines are unaffected by bending
Disjunctive onLine definition works better than if-then-else for case analysis
change tactic essential for exposing concrete Q values before linarith
Gap of 3/88 between bent-line value and beta's y-coordinate is the obstruction

approaches.name: Moulton plane over Q with explicit counterexample
approaches.description: Defined MLine inductive type, computed concrete triangle pair, proved non-collinearity by exhaustive case analysis

papers: Moulton, F.R. (1902). A Simple Non-Desarguesian Plane Geometry
